notes: Sourced from Zoom's official US product/spec page (zoomcorp.com/en/us/podtrak-recorders/podcast-recorders/podtrak-p4/). Desktop unit, no rack mounting (rackUnits omitted). 4 mic inputs are plain XLR (not combo XLR/TRS) per manufacturer spec table "MIC: XLR jacks (2: HOT)" — line-level input acceptance is not documented. The smartphone jack is a 4-conductor TRRS connector; mapped to the closest available connector id "trs-3.5" since TRRS is not a distinct option in the enum, and marked bidirectional since it both sends the mix to the phone and receives the caller's audio. Two separate USB-C ports exist: one for USB audio-interface/mass-storage (data, bidirectional) and one dedicated solely to power input (DC 5V/1A) — neither has a stated USB speed grade in the manufacturer spec, so "grade" was omitted per instructions rather than guessed. Power can alternatively come from 2x AA batteries (not a physical connector, so not listed as a port). No line-level audio outputs exist beyond the four independent 3.5mm headphone jacks.

ports.name: Phone (Smartphone TRRS)
ports.note: 4-contact TRRS mini jack (TIP:L, RING1:R, RING2:GND, SLEEVE:MIC) for phone call audio in/out; closest listed connector id is trs-3.5, actual jack is TRRS not 3-conductor TRS

ports.name: USB (Audio Interface / Mass Storage)
ports.note: USB-C, used for USB audio interface mode and SD card mass-storage file transfer; USB spec version (2.0/3.x) not stated by manufacturer, so no grade set

ports.name: USB-C (Power)
ports.note: Dedicated power-only USB-C port, DC 5V/1A; also runs on 2x AA batteries (not a connector)
